data.title: AgiBot and Lens Technology Deploy Dozens of Genie G2 Robots on Phone Testing Line
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Yicai, AgiBot Robotics and Lens Technology have reached a strategic partnership and deployed dozens of AgiBot Genie G2 robots on a mobile phone testing production line, reporters learned on November 20. The robots are handling tasks including loading and unloading test stations and interacting with testing equipment. The deployment covers phone MMI, ANT, CAM, and CAMCV testing, where roles involve repetitive operations and frequent model updates. AgiBot Robotics previously deployed robots at Longqi’s Nanchang factory.

data.description: According to Jin10, Automus announced a partnership with Google Cloud to help accelerate agentic transformation.

data.title: STOCKS | Bank of America Raises Strategy Stake to $160.7 Million With 688,560-Share Increase
data.description: Bank of America disclosed that it added 688,560 shares of Strategy, valued at $59.3 million. According to Odaily, the bank reported holding 1,865,485 shares worth $160.7 million, up 59% from its previous position.

data.title: UK and EU Reach Post-Brexit Deal Package, but Tuition Fee Dispute Remains
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, the United Kingdom and the European Union have agreed on a series of deals to deepen post-Brexit ties, though they remain divided over tuition fees. The agreements are intended to facilitate food trade, link their carbon markets, and allow young people to live, work and study in the other party’s country. A UK official said the timing of the agreements’ implementation would be set out in an upcoming joint statement.

Finalizing the post-Brexit agreements was a main goal of Friday’s summit in Brussels between UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and EU leaders. A last-minute impasse over tuition fees raised questions about whether implementation could be delayed. The EU has sought local-student tuition rates for EU students studying in the UK.

The core elements of the agreements had been widely disclosed during months of negotiations, which were delayed after Burnham’s predecessor, Keir Starmer, resigned. Burnham said the agreements could increase UK economic output by 0.4%.

data.title: CATL, Luxshare to Enter Hang Seng Tech Index in Expansion

data.title: Doubao Work Cuts Usage Multipliers for Two Models to 0.01
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Dachang Ribao, Doubao Work lowered usage multipliers for several models, including DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Doubao 2.1 Lite, which are now set at 0.01. Simple conversations and low-consumption tasks are free. In the outlet’s tests, more than 80% of 50 office tasks run with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash incurred no charge; a 3D modeling task cost about RMB 0.23, and generating a dynamic webpage cost about RMB 0.06. Doubao Work also added Kimi K3.1 Pro and GLM 5.3 among its third-party models.

data.title: Google Stock Nears 2025 Valuation Bottom as Larry Williams Sees Rally Signals
data.description: Google stock closed at $272.66 on November 19, down nearly 20% in a month, as veteran chartist Larry Williams identified two signals that could point to a rally. The shares trade at roughly 15 times 2026 earnings estimates, near their valuation level at the spring 2025 bottom, according to BeInCrypto. Alphabet’s third-quarter earnings on October 28 showed Search revenue growth slowing to 12% from 17% in the second quarter, below analyst forecasts, and GOOGL fell more than 12% the next day, its worst post-earnings drop on record. Concerns that AI Mode could threaten Search weighed on the stock even as Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7 billion. Broader selling in AI-linked stocks helped drive a $2.2 trillion market rout on November 16. Williams’ two indicators—one tracking professional accumulation and another flagging potentially undervalued stocks—have both turned positive, with large investors accumulating Alphabet shares over the past four weeks. A similar setup appeared earlier in 2026 ahead of a sharp rally. Jim Cramer shared Williams’ charts on CNBC on Thursday. In April 2025, Alphabet traded near 16.9 times forward earnings, the cheapest of the Magnificent Seven, per Zacks; shares later more than doubled in just over a year after earnings showed Google’s AI features were lifting ad sales, Reuters reported. The current setup faces higher investment costs: Alphabet set a $75 billion capital spending plan for 2025 in February 2025 and now guides for $195 billion to $205 billion in 2026, mostly for AI infrastructure, with spending expected to rise significantly again in 2027. Third-quarter capital spending was $51.4 billion, while free cash flow was negative $9.1 billion as spending and inventory costs rose. A Bank of America survey found fund managers rank an AI bubble as the top market risk. A repeat of the 2025 rebound may depend on Search growth stabilizing as spending increases.

data.title: Anthropic Rolls Out New Products, Deepens Discounts to Support $1.5 Trillion Valuation
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Anthropic is expanding beyond coding with new AI products and offering large customers discounts to support its fully diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion. The company priced its IPO at $83 per share on Wednesday evening, above the previous week’s indicated range of $70 to $78, ahead of its Thursday listing.

Anthropic’s first-quarter revenue this year rose to $4.7 billion, exceeding its total for last year. Second-quarter revenue increased a further 144%, while third-quarter revenue grew 47% quarter over quarter to $17 billion. The company has not broken out revenue by product or industry, and customers and advisers say Claude Code still accounts for most spending. Anthropic says Claude Cowork’s user adoption after nine months exceeded Claude Code’s, which launched in February 2025, but it did not provide figures.

Anthropic has introduced tools including Claude Cowork, Claude Managed Agents, Claude Security, Claude Design and Claude Science, and tailored Claude products for seven industries. Customers are also using its models for cybersecurity tasks, though many access them through their own orchestration frameworks rather than Claude Security. Claude Managed Agents remains in public testing.

Customers said Anthropic is offering some large accounts discounts above 30%, generally in exchange for commitments to direct a share of their overall AI budgets to the company. Some contracts require customers to provide documents to verify those commitments. Anthropic has also offered product credits, including up to $100,000 for some customers and up to $2,000 per user for trials of newly launched tools. Customers said they are monitoring rising bills and may reduce usage.

OpenAI is also discounting its products, with some reported discounts of 20% to 30% and one Codex deal at 40%. Vertice CEO Eldar Tuvey said companies have expanded Claude use from engineering teams to sales, finance, human resources and marketing.

data.title: Fluid Partners With Anchorage Digital to Enable USDC Lending and hBTC-Collateralized Borrowing on Sui
data.description: Fluid has integrated with Anchorage Digital, a U.S.-licensed digital asset bank, giving the bank’s institutional clients access to Fluid’s lending markets on Sui. According to Foresight News, clients can lend USDC on the protocol to earn yield or borrow USDC against hBTC, a Bitcoin-backed asset minted through Sui-native Bitcoin finance infrastructure Hashi.

data.title: Tej Johar: SK Hynix U.S. Share Premium Could Narrow
data.description: According to CNBC, Tej Johar, a portfolio manager at Trium Capital, is betting that SK Hynix’s U.S.-listed shares will lose part of their premium to equivalent securities in Seoul and Frankfurt. The premium widened from 13% to about 48% after the company listed on Nasdaq via American depositary receipts in July, as U.S. investors sought exposure to AI companies, Johar said. On Nov. 13, Seoul- and Frankfurt-listed securities closed at about $90, compared with $132 for the U.S. shares. Johar said the typical American depositary receipt premium over the past 25 years was about zero and described the potential trade as an approximately $8 billion alpha opportunity.

data.title: Euro-Area Pay Growth Edged Up Marginally in Third Quarter
data.description: A key measure of euro-area pay growth accelerated only slightly in the third quarter, reassuring the European Central Bank that inflation triggered by rising energy prices is not spreading, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Bending Spoons May Issue Convertible Bonds as Supplementary Funding
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, a person familiar with Bending Spoons said the company is considering issuing convertible bonds as a supplement to its existing funding channels amid high interest rates. Such bonds generally carry lower coupons than conventional bonds of similar ratings, but give bondholders the option to convert them into shares, diluting existing shareholders.

Since listing in July, Bending Spoons has raised funds through debt and equity markets, mainly to acquire more technology companies and operate its expanding portfolio. Its acquisitions include AOL, Eventbrite, Airtable and Vimeo. The company is betting that major restructuring can revive growth at these established brands. Its latest acquisition, collaboration software company Miro, closed in late October at an enterprise valuation of about $1.36 billion, 90% below Miro’s valuation in a 2021 private funding round.

People familiar with the company said past acquisitions typically cost one to seven times the target’s revenue. Bending Spoons is now targeting companies with annual revenue of at least $500 million and deal values in the multibillion-dollar range. It is open to acquisitions across technology, with health technology a particular area of interest. Acquisitions are funded mainly with debt, supplemented by free cash flow and equity. In the first six months of 2026, the company generated about $250 million in free cash flow, compared with $2.3 billion in total acquisition spending.

Bending Spoons aims to keep net leverage at two to three times. At the end of June, net debt was $4.09 billion and leverage was about 2.4 times. The company is due to report third-quarter results this Friday. Moody’s and S&P have assigned it non-investment-grade credit ratings. It secured about $1.7 billion in loans in September, partly to finance the Miro deal, and raised $1.8 billion in its first high-yield bond sale in October. A person familiar with the matter put the blended effective rate on its debt at about 9%.

The company’s funding costs could fall modestly as it builds a public-company track record or if overall interest rates decline. An investment-grade rating could lower borrowing costs further, but would require reduced leverage or other trade-offs; the company has no current plan to pursue that, a source said. Bending Spoons views convertible bonds as supplementary, not a core funding source, because they cannot raise very large sums and the company wants to limit dilution.

Last month, Bending Spoons privately placed $330 million in shares with Berkshire Hathaway, which had invested $600 million in its IPO. Equity issuance helps keep leverage within its target ceiling. After acquisitions, the company lays off employees and assigns 50 to 60 of its own staff to management roles. It has also raised prices at several acquired companies, but has no current plan to raise prices at Airtable, acquired in September.

data.title: Hong Kong Proposes SFC Licensing for Four Types of Virtual Asset Services
data.description: Hong Kong’s government has gazetted the Draft 2026 Virtual Asset Service Legislation (Amendment) Bill. According to Odaily, the proposal would bring virtual asset trading, advisory, management and custody services under licensing or registration by the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC); providers would need to meet fit-and-proper criteria. Banks regulated by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and licensed stored-value facility operators would also need to register with the SFC to provide any virtual asset services in Hong Kong. The bill is scheduled for its first reading in the Legislative Council on December 2.

data.description: According to Jin10, the Saudi Press Agency reported that Japan plans to buy 8 million barrels of crude oil from Saudi Arabia to replenish its national oil reserves.

data.title: Joerg Wuttke: Putin's First Trilateral Meeting Was a Major Win
data.description: According to CNBC, Russian President Vladimir Putin joined U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping for their first-ever trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit Thursday. Joerg Wuttke of DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group said Putin emerged with stronger standing and described the meeting as a major win for the Russian leader. Putin also held bilateral meetings with at least seven world leaders over the two days, while the war in Ukraine continued with no signs of ending. The three leaders issued a joint declaration of peace, but no concrete agreements on Ukraine were announced. Andrius Tursa, a Teneo adviser, said Putin would likely seek to make the trilateral format permanent.

data.title: AI | Minerva Uses Chinese Open-Weight Models for Specific Use Cases
data.description:
Minerva mixes and matches AI models for specific use cases, co-founder Daniel Saedi said in an interview, according to Bloomberg. He also discussed data sovereignty and the risk of “obliterated models.”

This week, the Trump administration was reportedly considering requiring US companies to disclose publicly whether they use Chinese AI models. Last year, a Chinese company released a cheaper model that appeared nearly as capable as cutting-edge US models, in what became known as the “DeepSeek moment.”

data.title: AI | US Chip Curbs Stir Fresh Volatility Around Nvidia
data.description:
The US imposed new restrictions on China’s access to high-end AI chips after a spying controversy involving Nvidia, setting off fresh volatility in the AI trade during a choppy week for equities, Bloomberg reported.

The curbs threatened a fragile trade truce as President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump met at the APEC leaders’ summit in Shenzhen. Investors also weighed questions about how a leadership shift at Nvidia and global AI policy could affect semiconductor supply chains.
